ci_pipeline.note: GitHub Actions job durations on run for commit bcf9fbce (v8.3.0).

before.cause: 289 suites ran serially on ONE runner

ci_pipeline.safety: tests/test-shard-coverage.sh (14/14) proves the shards partition the suite list exactly and that an invalid shard spec exits non-zero rather than silently running nothing.

local_shard_measurement.note: Local Mac timing for ONE shard, executed end to end. Confirms the split runs and passes; it is NOT the CI number, since runners are slower than this machine.

MEASURED_after.note: OBSERVED CI timings, replacing the earlier ~195s projection. The real number is 335s, not 195s: shards are uneven because suite cost varies, so the wall clock is the SLOWEST shard, not the mean. The projection assumed even cost and was optimistic.

green_run.note: First fully green sharded run. The two failures on the prior commit were latent bugs the sharding EXPOSED (a skip that exited 1; stderr folded into a JSON stream), both fixed in v8.3.1 -- not regressions caused by sharding.
